lines: Welcome to Mulberry's. The Post-Mortem is in the rack by the door. A dollar eighty-one, plus tax.
I ring it up with two fingers now. The other eight are in a sandwich bag in the ice case, in case somebody can sew them back on.
You did it. You know this town better than anybody who's shambled in here all year.
Mulberry's Hometown Hero. I'll put your picture by the register, next to the missing posters.
We sponsor the Beach Dads' pancake breakfast every year. Us, Piedmont Grocery and Village Market.
Three markets, one very sticky blacktop. This year the Beach Dads brought their own batter, and nobody has asked what's in it.
We're always looking for a Hometown Hero. Somebody who really knows this town and still has a pulse.
Fill up that journal of yours and come tell me. Before you turn, ideally.
Hometown Hero! Your picture's going up any day now. Soon as I find the tape, and my other hand.

lines: Jay Russell, the Post-Mortem. The Question Man asks a prescient question each week at an unannounced location. Lately, wherever I'm hiding.
This week: what do you think about kids riding e-bikes around town? It is the fastest way out of a horde.

choices.label: Good for outrunning things.
reply: Ella and Evie said the same thing. 'We think they look fun.' They said it pedaling away from me.

choices.label: Children on motorcycles.
reply: That's what Christina Maybaum told me. 'Essentially it's children on motorcycles.' Today that's an evacuation plan.

choices.label: Helmets. Protect the brain.
reply: Britt McCormick thinks helmets should come in the box. Everybody in town wants your brain right now. Cover it.

choices.label: I wish they'd slow down.
reply: Judy Sokoloff said that, word for word. The dead would like them slower too. They can't keep up.

lines: If you entered a competitive eating contest, what would you eat? Most of the town has already entered.

choices.label: Steak.
reply: A seventh grader told me steak. 'Even when I was little, I could always eat a lot of steak.' He's moved on to rarer things.

choices.label: Hot chicken pho.
reply: Two third graders, same answer. Great minds. Everybody's after great minds lately.

choices.label: A hundred strawberries.
reply: A third grader told me she could eat a hundred. I believe her. Strawberries are the only red thing in town I still trust.

choices.label: Marshmallows.
reply: A man told me he won a marshmallow contest in high school while choking on one.
'No one was paying attention so I still won.' Please don't do that. Stop breathing in this town and people notice for the wrong reasons.

lines: Last question of the season. What was your first car?

lines.text: I don't have my permit yet.

lines: Every car in town has its keys in it right now, and nobody left to check.
Then you've got a head start on the man whose first car was a 1958 Edsel he bought for three hundred dollars. He's still sitting in it. It still won't start.
Quoted in the Post-Mortem three times now. Most people only make it in once, in the back pages.
I'll find you next week. I always do. Unannounced location. Lock your windows.

entries.name: PPD Blue

lines: PPD BLUE. Every week the Piedmont police still post a Pick of the Week: the strangest call in town. Runner-up: 'Neighbor eating other neighbor. Officer advised it was a civil matter.'
There are 11 picks this year, and every one happened somewhere in Piedmont. Find all 11 scenes.
Find one and the next pick goes up. No need to walk back here: your Journal (J) always shows the latest pick.
This week's pick is in your Journal now. Press J. The officer who pins these up has fewer thumbs every week.
PPD BLUE. PICK OF THE WEEK: 'Holy buzzcut, Batman.' A bat dive-bombing people. It was already dead when it started. WHERE: Dracena Park, in the dog park just north of Blair's Quarry.
PPD BLUE. PICK OF THE WEEK: 'Found bound hound sound.' A big gray and white dog stuck between two walls. Dog fine. Walls under investigation. WHERE: Grand Ave, up near Greenbank Ave.
PPD BLUE. PICK OF THE WEEK: 'How a bus does a wheelie.' A visiting team's bus stuck on three wheels. The team is still on it. Do not knock. WHERE: the entrance to Witter Field. Look for a tilted bus.

PPD BLUE. PICK OF THE WEEK: 'Just hit it.' Wasps attacking dogs. An officer checks. The hedge has started hitting back. WHERE: walk straight south from the Brick Maze House to Hampton Rd, then follow Sandringham Rd to an officer and a buzzing hedge.
PPD BLUE. PICK OF THE WEEK: 'Too early for Santa.' People up on a roof in September. They are still up there, and they are right not to come down. WHERE: Linda Ave, east of Hugo's house on Olive.

PPD BLUE. PICK OF THE WEEK: 'What do teens without ebikes do?' Teens getting cars to honk at them. Honking draws the dead. The teens call that a feature. WHERE: San Carlos Ave, between Magnolia and Oakland Ave, west of the Middle School.

PPD BLUE. PICK OF THE WEEK: 'Can we keep it, pleeease?' A small white dog with no collar at Wildwood Elementary. Dogs are immune. He's the healthiest thing at the school. WHERE: the dog is at the school. His owner is on Wildwood Ave, just east of it.
PPD BLUE. PICK OF THE WEEK: 'Not going to win that one.' An SUV versus a garbage truck. The truck is still collecting. Nobody is driving it. WHERE: Prospect Rd, southeast of Wildwood Elementary.

PPD BLUE. PICK OF THE WEEK: 'Burning Man? No, no, just a road trip.' Somebody packing a beach cruiser into a tiny car at 2 a.m. The cruiser was not the only thing going in. WHERE: a driveway on Oakland Ave, just north of Havens Elementary.
PPD BLUE. PICK OF THE WEEK: 'Uber Eats or EMT?' A man called an ambulance because he was hungry. The EMTs got there. He was still hungry. WHERE: Highland Ave, outside the Community Hall.

PPD BLUE. PICK OF THE WEEK: 'MHS Falcon Hour during summer?' A 'falcon' in a school cafeteria, eating better than anyone else in there. WHERE: Piedmont Middle School on Magnolia Ave. Ask the custodian out front.
PPD BLUE. You've seen every Pick of the Week this year. The officers are a little worried about you. The ones who still have faces.

entries.name: Princess Donut
entries.title: Park Way

lines: YOU MAY APPROACH. SLOWLY. MY COURT IS EATING.
I AM PRINCESS DONUT. FORMER GRAND CHAMPION, CURRENT QUEEN OF PARK WAY, AND I HAVE ONE POINT TWO MILLION FOLLOWERS.
THESE ARE MY STAFF. I RAISED THEM WITH SECOND CHANCE. THEY ARE TERRIBLE AT EVERYTHING EXCEPT KNEELING.
AND YOU HAVE... BROCCOLI ON YOUR HEAD. FASCINATING. IS THAT A CHOICE?
DO NOT LET THOSE DOGS NEAR ME. THE SMALL ONE LOOKED AT ME. I FELT IT.
MONGO IS LOOSE. HE ATE A MAIL CARRIER, THREW HIM UP, AND ATE HIM AGAIN. MONGO IS APPALLED!
SIXTEEN? UGH. I WAS A GRAND CHAMPION BEFORE I WAS ONE. TRY HARDER.

entries.name: Cheddar
entries.title: Captain Holt's dog

lines: A corgi in a tiny police vest. His tag says CHEDDAR.
Cheddar regards you with total professionalism. He is the only officer at the station who has not tried to bite anyone.
Detective Cheddar has found a femur and will not be taking questions.
BONE?!
You try to pet Cheddar. He allows it, once. Do not get comfortable.
